canonical_basis.hz4_invariant: STREAM routing preserves the existing canonical work/source/current/protocol split through RoyaltyRouter420 and RoyaltyVault420
canonical_basis.supported_class_policy: Only RecordingClass values with explicit canonical split terms already retained by the audited kernel are initialized. No unsupported class inherits or invents STREAM economics.

routing_preconditions: RoyaltyRouter420.setSettlementSource(StreamingRoyaltySettlement420,true) is already owned and retained by HZ-AUDIT-2/HZ-AUDIT-3
Recording royaltyScheduleVersion must equal 1 for these STREAM v1 schedules
StreamingRoyaltySettlement420 routes only RevenueType.STREAM with exact allocated value
RoyaltyRouter420 requires the schedule to exist and be effective before routing
safety_invariants: Every schedule sums to exactly 10000 basis points.
Protocol fee remains 250 bps and therefore does not exceed the 500 bps kernel cap.
ORIGINAL has zero source share because ORIGINAL recordings cannot have a parent recording.
REMIX preserves the canonical one-hop 1500 bps immediate-source share.
Schedule version 1 is immutable once registered; duplicate registration must fail.
Terms hashes commit the complete split, version, effective-at value, class and STREAM revenue type.
Unsupported RecordingClass values have no STREAM schedule and fail closed at RoyaltyScheduleRegistry420/RoyaltyRouter420 rather than receiving invented economics.
No local initialization result is promoted to live/testnet transaction evidence.
exit_criteria: supported STREAM RecordingClass inventory is explicit and repository-grounded
version 1 ORIGINAL and REMIX STREAM schedules preserve the canonical split terms
effective-at values are exact and deterministic
terms hashes commit every economic field and schedule identity field
governance-only registration and duplicate/version replay behavior are focused-tested
real RoyaltyRouter420 STREAM routing conserves exact gross value under both supported schedules
unsupported RecordingClass values fail closed without invented economics
